archetypes.name: fixture-spec
archetypes.rationale: The Case 2 dynamic test's pass/fail outcome depends entirely on fixture file content the plan leaves underspecified — a wrong fixture shape causes test failure for the wrong reason rather than validating the portability fix.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect skills/design/scripts/render-final-summary.sh to determine every file it reads when invoked with --post-publish-only and a non-cancelled-outline outcome (e.g., 'approved'). Cross-check the plan's listed fixture files (run-params.json, voting-tally.md, accepted-plan-findings.md, oos-accepted-design.md, execution-issues.md, oos-issues-created.md) against what the script actually reads at runtime, including any required field values within those files (e.g., mode, outcome, or cost fields in run-params.json). Identify any fixture file or required field whose schema the plan does not specify but the script requires for rc=0, where a missing or malformed value would cause the script to fail on a reason entirely unrelated to the Bash 3.2 nounset hazard. Also check whether skills/design/scripts/test-render-final-summary.sh's existing fixture can be reused directly or needs adaptation for the --post-publish-only invocation path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shard-registry
archetypes.rationale: The plan picks test-harnesses-12 with a fallback to test-harnesses-14 without verifying current Makefile shard contents — a wrong placement silently omits the new test from make lint.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the Makefile and identify the current dependency lists for test-harnesses-12 and test-harnesses-14, including the exact targets each shard depends on and whether test-collect-agent-bash32 actually lives in test-harnesses-14 as the plan claims. Verify whether test-harnesses-12 currently hosts test-render-final-summary, test-render-run-summary, test-render-cost-line, and test-render-run-summary-callsites as the plan asserts. Determine whether the plan's chosen shard (test-harnesses-12) is accurate, and check whether a shard balance constraint would redirect placement to test-harnesses-14 instead. Also verify that the plan's .PHONY placement instruction and target-rule insertion point ('after the existing test-render-final-summary rule, line ~468') match the actual Makefile line structure, so the implementer does not insert the target in the wrong location. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: precedent-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan tells the implementer to mirror scripts/test-collect-agent-bash32.sh but does not enumerate which structural patterns are required vs optional, leaving the implementer to guess and potentially miss key invariants that the static-grep case must encode.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/test-collect-agent-bash32.sh in full and extract the exact structural patterns the plan directs the implementer to mirror: set header flags, PASS/FAIL/SKIP/FAILED globals, TMPROOT with trap, bash version-detection method and version-comparison arithmetic, loud-skip message format, ok/fail/skipm accounting helpers or inline equivalents, and the final summary line. Cross-check each pattern against the plan's Case 1 and Case 2 descriptions to identify any pattern the plan omits or underspecifies. Pay particular attention to whether the plan's Case 1 grep pattern is concrete enough (literal regex given vs described-only) and whether the plan's version-detection approach matches the actual pattern in the precedent file. Also verify that the plan's instruction to use 'two greps wired with &&' for all three guarded sites is consistent with pinning render_cost_args, note_args, and COST_ARGS separately — confirm whether three separate greps are needed or two suffice. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
